Geography & The Map of Naritonine

Seven continents and a scatter of island systems, twice the size of Earth's own land area. This section is the map itself, the water and land it names, and the scale behind every distance a tribe might travel.

The known world of Naritonine. Two labels on the original art were illegible in generation. The narrow strait at the Frostcrown/Emberspine land bridge, just north of the Ember Strait, is named here as The Amberlight Narrows; the inland landmark within The Long Shore as Vicolt. Both are original names, not misreadings of anything else on the map.

The Seven Continents

1 The Frostcrown

Glacier · Taiga · Alpine Tundra · Steppe · Fjord Coast

The world's northern crown, and its largest continent by far. Its coast is a maze of fjords cutting deep into the ice; inland, taiga gives way to open steppe before the true glacier begins. A single mountain range runs south from its heart, narrowing at last into the land bridge that ties it to Highgreen — the only place on the map where a person could, in principle, walk from permanent ice to tropical rainforest without once crossing open water.

Area: ~28.9M mi² (74.9M km²) Comparable to: Roughly Africa + Europe combined Crossing time: ~41 weeks, coast to coast Tribe capacity: ~35-45 tribes

2 Highgreen

Forest · Giant-Tree Forest · Rainforest · Cloud Forest · Cold High-Altitude Desert · Mountain · Plains · River Valleys

The most biome-diverse continent on the map, built around the southern continuation of the same spine that crowns the Frostcrown. Its highest peaks run cold and nearly desert-dry despite the tropical latitude; descending, the range passes through cloud forest, giant-tree forest, and true rainforest before finally opening into plains and river valleys near the coast.

Area: ~32.9M mi² (85.2M km²) Comparable to: About 3.5x Russia — roughly a third of Earth's entire land surface, in one continent Crossing time: ~44 weeks, pole to coast Tribe capacity: ~55-70 tribes

3 The Long Shore

Bamboo Forest · Terraced Farmland · Foothills · Hillocks · Meadow · Coastal

The most cultivated continent on the map, and the longest unbroken coastline of any of the eight. Generations of terracing have shaped its foothills into farmland; gentler, mountain-free hillocks roll further inland, and bamboo forest and open meadow fill in whatever the terraces haven't claimed. This is a continent shaped as much by hands as by weather.

Area: ~15.0M mi² (38.8M km²) Comparable to: Comparable to Asia Crossing time: ~30 weeks along its length Tribe capacity: ~40-55 tribes

4 The Cradle Basin

Desert · Sand Sea · Canyon · Salt Flats · High Plateau · Ringed Wetland Valley

A true desert core — dune sea, canyon country, a high wind-scoured plateau, salt flats bleached white — entirely encircled by a mountain range that traps what little water reaches it. That trapped water pools into a genuine wetland valley at the continent's heart: true desert on the outside, true wetland at the very center. A narrow land bridge at its southern edge carries the same dry geology onward into the Dryheart.

Area: ~11.0M mi² (28.5M km²) Comparable to: Comparable to North America Crossing time: ~27 weeks, rim to rim Tribe capacity: ~40-55 tribes

5 The Emberspine

Volcanic Spine · Geothermal Fields · Mangrove Coast · Karst · Cave Systems

A volcanic mountain chain runs the length of this continent, active at one end and long dormant at the other — geothermal geyser fields mark the middle ground between. Mangrove crowds its warm coastline; where the old, weathered end of the spine has finally gone quiet, karst country and true inhabited cave systems have had centuries to form.

Area: ~7.5M mi² (19.4M km²) Comparable to: Comparable to Australia, but long and narrow rather than compact Crossing time: ~28 weeks tip to tip, ~4.5 weeks across Tribe capacity: ~35-45 tribes

6 The Silt Kingdom

Swamp · Mangrove · Peat Bog · Salt Marsh · River Delta · Meadow Highground

The smallest of the seven true continents, and the lowest — built around a single massive river delta. Swamp, mangrove, peat bog, and salt marsh dominate the lowlands; whatever high ground rises above the silt has been claimed as meadow and settled farmland. Nothing here is far from water.

Area: ~4.5M mi² (11.6M km²) Comparable to: Comparable to Antarctica Crossing time: ~17 weeks Tribe capacity: ~40-55 tribes

7 The Dryheart

Desert-Scrub Core · Prairie · Savannah · River · Tropical Coast

Where the Cradle Basin's aridity crosses the isthmus and softens. Tropical and temperate coastline rings its outer edge, giving way to a dry, scrub-and-desert heart at the center. Prairie and savannah form the transition zone between wet coast and dry interior, and a single major river cuts clean across the continent.

Area: ~9.5M mi² (24.6M km²) Comparable to: Comparable to South America Crossing time: ~25 weeks Tribe capacity: ~35-45 tribes

Named Water Bodies

The Frostfjord Reach

The maze of deep fjords cutting into the Frostcrown's northern coast, the world's northernmost navigable water.

The Greenward Sea

The open water cupped between Frostcrown's coast, the Ash Archipelago's volcanic islands, and Highgreen's northern shore — named for the green land it opens onto.

The Ashmist Narrows

The narrow passage entering the Greenward Sea from the northwest, running between the Ash Archipelago's northernmost island and Frostcrown's coast — the mirror counterpart to the Ash Archipelago Channel, which enters the same sea from the northeast.

The Ash Archipelago Channel

The channel threading through the Ash Archipelago's volcanic islands, entering the Greenward Sea from the northeast, connecting toward the waters east of Highgreen.

The Ember Strait

The strait running along the Emberspine's eastern coast, named for the volcanic glow often visible from the water at night.

The Ember Sound

The calmer sound at the Emberspine's southern tip, distinct from the Ember Strait to its north, sheltered enough for real settlement.

The Silt Lagoons

The lagoon system spanning Highgreen's southern river mouth and the Silt Kingdom's northern coast, brackish and rich with wetland life.

The Sickle Bay

The bay cupped inside The Long Shore's crescent-shaped coastline, among the calmest waters on the map.

The Spined Passage

The passage threading through the Spined Archipelago, connecting the Cradle Basin's waters to the Dryheart's.

The Waking Deep

The main connecting ocean at the heart of the map, named for the world's own origin myth — the land waking from stillness.

The Thousand Sea

The southern waters surrounding the Thousand Isles, named for the sheer number of islands scattered across it.

The Isle Scatter

The loose scatter of small islands south of the Thousand Isles, among the least mapped waters in the world.

The Amberlight Narrows

A narrow strait at the land bridge where Frostcrown's southern tip meets Emberspine's northern end, distinct from the Ember Strait just south of it — named for how the volcanic glow catches on the water there after dark.

World Totals

Seven continents: ~109.3M mi²
All islands, all categories: ~5.74M mi² · 7,236 total islands
Grand total land area: ~115.0M mi² (2× Earth's actual land area)
Tribe-viable islands (≥5 mi²): 619 — a resource ceiling, not a requirement. Fourteen are currently claimed; the rest remain real, mapped, and open for a wanderer's story or a future tribe.
